business_problem: ServiceNow wanted to lower support costs and improve efficiency without losing the personalized, high-touch experience customers expect from human support teams.
solution_summary: ServiceNow reworked its support organization on the ServiceNow AI Platform by combining Technology Provider Service Management, Customer Service Management workflows, AI Agents, and AI-driven knowledge generation. The team began with self-service and agent productivity use cases, using early access capabilities for case summarization, routing, and article generation inside the same support environment it runs as customer zero for TPSM. AI Agents now handle the first layer of self-service interactions, while automation categorizes and routes cases before human agents step in. The platform also turns resolved work into AI-generated knowledge content so self-service improves over time. ServiceNow is using that architecture to move from channel-based triage toward conversation-led support where AI attempts resolution first and people engage for empathy, exceptions, or complex issues.

solution_components.role: Handle self-service conversations and automate support tasks such as routing, categorization, and summarization.

solution_components.name: Customer Service Management
solution_components.role: Coordinates customer-support workflows that blend AI automation with human-agent handoff.

solution_components.name: Knowledge Management
solution_components.role: Stores and expands the support content that feeds self-service and automation.

data_flow: Customers start with self-service on AI Agents, which route, categorize, and summarize issues inside Technology Provider Service Management and Customer Service Management. When automation cannot complete the work, the platform hands a summarized case to a human agent, and successful resolutions are turned into AI-generated knowledge articles that strengthen the next self-service interaction.
business_outcome: AI and automation now support 89% of self-service requests, AI agents participate in 37% of case workflow, and 60% of knowledge articles are AI-generated, cutting average publishing time by 88% while preserving ServiceNow's hospitality-first support model.
